# Architecture decision records

This folder records the architectural decisions for `worthyd-game-tools`: what was decided and
why. The topic guides in [`docs/ai/`](../ai/README.md) say *how* to write code here; ADRs say
*what was decided*. State each rule once: if a guide needs a decision, it links to the ADR.

ADRs use the minimal [MADR 4](https://adr.github.io/madr/) template, with a few extra frontmatter
fields that feed the AI agent instructions.

## How agents use these

`npm run ai:sync` (`tools/ai/sync-ai-rules.mjs`) turns ADRs into agent context:

| ADR status | Where agents see it |
|---|---|
| `accepted` | One line in the **Architecture decisions** table in `AGENTS.md`, which Claude Code (via `CLAUDE.md`), Copilot (via `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) and the Copilot coding agent always load. If `globs` is set, the Decision Outcome is also generated into `.claude/rules/adr-*.md` and `.github/instructions/adr-*.instructions.md`, so it loads whenever an agent edits matching files. |
| `proposed` | This README only. Context, not binding. |
| `deprecated`, `superseded` | This README only. History; agents ignore them. |

`AGENTS.md` tells agents that accepted ADRs are binding, that they must stop and say so when a task
conflicts with one, and that a new architectural choice needs a proposed ADR.

## Writing an ADR

1. `npm run adr:new -- "Short decision title"` creates the next numbered file from
   [`adr-template.md`](adr-template.md) with `status: proposed`.
2. Fill in the sections. Keep it short: the current decision and enough reasoning to apply it.
   Git is the history, so don't keep amendment logs in the file.
3. Fill in the frontmatter:

   | Field | Meaning |
   |---|---|
   | `status` | `proposed`, `accepted`, `deprecated` or `superseded`. Only a human sets `accepted`. |
   | `date` | When the status last changed (`YYYY-MM-DD`). |
   | `decision-makers` | Who decided. |
   | `summary` | One sentence agents can follow without reading the rest. Required when accepted. |
   | `globs` | JSON array of paths the decision applies to, e.g. `["libs/craft-cart/**"]`. `[]` means everywhere (index line only). |
   | `enforced-by` | The lint rule or test that checks it, or `review`. |
   | `superseded-by` | The replacing ADR's number (`0012`). Required when superseded. |

   Don't put `#` comments in the frontmatter; the sync script reads values literally.

4. `npm run ai:sync`, then commit the ADR and the generated files together. CI runs
   `npm run ai:check` and fails if they're out of date.

## Changing a decision

Don't rewrite an accepted ADR's decision. Write a new ADR that supersedes it, then set the old one to
`status: superseded` and `superseded-by: NNNN`. Small clarifications that don't change the decision
can be edited in place.

## Enforcement

Prefer decisions a machine can check. If a lint rule (`@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`,
`no-restricted-imports`, an `@angular-eslint` rule) or a test can enforce the ADR, add it and name it
in `enforced-by` and the Confirmation section. Agents can miss prose, but `npx nx affected -t lint test build`
is part of their definition of done.
